trust_boundary: Controller-pinned manifest digest is a fixture trust anchor held outside the mutable store. It binds one selected generation; reader derives missing required events and snapshot content from bytes. This is not a production authentication scheme or protection against a compromised controller.
namespace_boundary: Only the selected committed generation is admitted for replay; old generation artifacts are retained as forensic evidence, not silently treated as replayable. Distinguish logical retirement from physical deletion. In-place removal exercises actual selected-namespace absence.
method: Compare independent fresh-process reader observations after named writer termination cuts. All inputs are synthetic. Interrupted or mixed facts must block or leave the previous coherent generation readable. Verify M1B wire independently of application installation.
limits: Finite named process-termination cuts on the admitted local filesystem; no power failure, arbitrary interleaving theorem, real provider or common-writer migration result.
next: Execute source-frozen prospective admission; retain failed attempts and named-cut receipts.

expected_dispositions.writer: Staged generation retains g1 replay at four prepublication cuts; in-place blocks at those cuts. Both admit g2 gap after commit_published. Complete update admits gap; baseline admits replay.
expected_dispositions.receiver: RESET_emitted and snapshot_staged leave committed application A/cursor1; reset_committed leaves Aé/cursor2. All reopen to AéB/cursor3 and repeat attachment emits no event. Literal accepted-reset at each cut does not assert application recovery.
expected_dispositions.controls: hole-prefix accepts gap; retained-suffix accepts replay; all remaining controls reject evidence or refuse receiver before wire emission.

cleanup: Wait every owned helper handle, close pipes; retain all isolated fixture bytes as forensic evidence. No running service or outside temporary files.
measurement: Named-cut outcomes and helper counts, not performance benchmarks. Parent trace records actual PID, exit, phases, fresh reader nonce and observed file digests.
